"PROJECT: \"Cat Lineage\" (working title) — a tactical cat-breeding roguelite

Build a playable browser game (HTML5 + TypeScript/JS; Phaser 3, PixiJS or plain Canvas, your choice) that recreates the core design of Mewgenics (Edmund McMillen and Tyler Glaiel, released Feb 10, 2026). This is a personal fan-style prototype. Reproduce the SYSTEMS, structure and FEEL, but make all art, audio, text and character names ORIGINAL. Do not copy or trace the original game's assets or lines. Support desktop mouse and mobile touch.

HOW TO WORK
- Start with a short plan and list your assumptions. Don't ask me questions; decide and document.
- Build in the milestone order at the bottom. After each milestone, run it, fix bugs, and tell me what is done and what is stubbed.
- Make everything data-driven (JSON for classes, abilities, items, statuses, tiles, enemies, events, furniture). Keep simulation logic in pure functions, separate from rendering. Use a seeded RNG.
- Put every tunable constant in one config file.

1. THE PITCH AND CORE LOOP
You move into a small fictional town (call it \"Boon County\") and raise a lineage of cats in a cluttered house. The game has two halves:
- HOUSE (management and breeding sim): place furniture, feed cats, let them breed and fight overnight, manage room stats.
- ADVENTURE (turn-based tactics roguelite): send a party of 1-4 adult cats through chapters of battles, events, shops and bosses.
Loop: breed -> assign class collars and equip items -> adventure -> loot -> cats that return become RETIRED (cannot adventure again) -> donate cats to NPCs for permanent upgrades -> breed the next generation. If the whole party dies, all cats, items and resources on that run are lost.
Tone: dark, crude, absurd humor (poop jokes, grotesque mutations, deadpan NPCs), but cats stay expressive and endearing. Keep it PG-13: breeding happens off-screen as a cheeky text log (\"X got together with Y and made a kitten!\"), with no explicit animation.

2. ART DIRECTION (very important)
Reference: Edmund McMillen's The Binding of Isaac, Super Meat Boy and The End Is Nigh, and Newgrounds-era Flash cartoons (Clubby the Seal, the Obituary-era look). The game is described as crude, Flash-animated vector art with bold lines and bulbous, grotesque-but-cute characters. Reviewers also note a mostly black-and-white feel with small color accents.
- Linework: thick, slightly wobbly black outlines, uneven line weight, hand-drawn imperfection. Add a subtle line-wobble effect.
- Shapes: bulbous, rubbery, over-round bodies; huge expressive eyes and eyebrows; stubby limbs; weird-but-readable silhouettes.
- Animation: Flash-style puppet rigs. Cats are built from swappable vector parts (body, head, tail, legs, arms, eyes, eyebrows, ears, mouth, fur texture) with tweened squash-and-stretch, idle breathing, blinking and exaggerated hit reactions. Boss animations should feel slick and bigger than normal enemies.
- Palette: dingy paper off-white (#EDE6D6), soot black (#151210), dried-blood red (#B3261E), bile yellow (#D9B84A), sickly green (#7C8F3A), bruise purple (#5B3A6B). Use mostly desaturated backgrounds and let color pop on cats, status effects and hazards.
- House: cozy cross-section rooms crammed with junk furniture, with a radio, food bowls and litter.
- Battle: a readable 10x10 tile grid with clean icons. Tile types need distinct silhouettes and colors, because bold lines and bulbous characters can make the board hard to read.
- Mutations visibly change body parts (extra eyes, weird ears, bandaged mouths, odd tails).
- NOT: clean corporate flat vector, glossy 3D, pixel art, anime.
Audio and tone: each chapter gets its own energetic, melodic, genre-hopping theme with a punny title, and the house has a radio station with unlockable tracks. Use WebAudio-generated or original placeholder loops. Add rubbery cat voices with per-cat pitch.

3. CATS
Seven stats: STR, DEX, CON, INT, CHA, SPD, LCK. Base stats range 3-7 (5 is neutral)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

PROJECT: "Cat Lineage" (working title) — a tactical cat-breeding roguelite

Build a playable browser game (HTML5 + TypeScript/JS; Phaser 3, PixiJS or plain Canvas, your choice) that recreates the core design of Mewgenics (Edmund McMillen and Tyler Glaiel, released Feb 10, 2026). This is a personal fan-style prototype. Reproduce the SYSTEMS, structure and FEEL, but make all art, audio, text and character names ORIGINAL. Do not copy or trace the original game's assets or lines. Support desktop mouse and mobile touch.


HOW TO WORK
- Start with a short plan and list your assumptions. Don't ask me questions; decide and document.
- Build in the milestone order at the bottom. After each milestone, run it, fix bugs, and tell me what is done and what is stubbed.
- Make everything data-driven (JSON for classes, abilities, items, statuses, tiles, enemies, events, furniture). Keep simulation logic in pure functions, separate from rendering. Use a seeded RNG.
- Put every tunable constant in one config file.


1. THE PITCH AND CORE LOOP
You move into a small fictional town (call it "Boon County") and raise a lineage of cats in a cluttered house. The game has two halves:
- HOUSE (management and breeding sim): place furniture, feed cats, let them breed and fight overnight, manage room stats.
- ADVENTURE (turn-based tactics roguelite): send a party of 1-4 adult cats through chapters of battles, events, shops and bosses.
Loop: breed -> assign class collars and equip items -> adventure -> loot -> cats that return become RETIRED (cannot adventure again) -> donate cats to NPCs for permanent upgrades -> breed the next generation. If the whole party dies, all cats, items and resources on that run are lost.
Tone: dark, crude, absurd humor (poop jokes, grotesque mutations, deadpan NPCs), but cats stay expressive and endearing. Keep it PG-13: breeding happens off-screen as a cheeky text log ("X got together with Y and made a kitten!"), with no explicit animation.


2. ART DIRECTION (very important)
Reference: Edmund McMillen's The Binding of Isaac, Super Meat Boy and The End Is Nigh, and Newgrounds-era Flash cartoons (Clubby the Seal, the Obituary-era look). The game is described as crude, Flash-animated vector art with bold lines and bulbous, grotesque-but-cute characters. Reviewers also note a mostly black-and-white feel with small color accents.
- Linework: thick, slightly wobbly black outlines, uneven line weight, hand-drawn imperfection. Add a subtle line-wobble effect.
- Shapes: bulbous, rubbery, over-round bodies; huge expressive eyes and eyebrows; stubby limbs; weird-but-readable silhouettes.
- Animation: Flash-style puppet rigs. Cats are built from swappable vector parts (body, head, tail, legs, arms, eyes, eyebrows, ears, mouth, fur texture) with tweened squash-and-stretch, idle breathing, blinking and exaggerated hit reactions. Boss animations should feel slick and bigger than normal enemies.
- Palette: dingy paper off-white (#EDE6D6), soot black (#151210), dried-blood red (#B3261E), bile yellow (#D9B84A), sickly green (#7C8F3A), bruise purple (#5B3A6B). Use mostly desaturated backgrounds and let color pop on cats, status effects and hazards.
- House: cozy cross-section rooms crammed with junk furniture, with a radio, food bowls and litter.
- Battle: a readable 10x10 tile grid with clean icons. Tile types need distinct silhouettes and colors, because bold lines and bulbous characters can make the board hard to read.
- Mutations visibly change body parts (extra eyes, weird ears, bandaged mouths, odd tails).
- NOT: clean corporate flat vector, glossy 3D, pixel art, anime.
Audio and tone: each chapter gets its own energetic, melodic, genre-hopping theme with a punny title, and the house has a radio station with unlockable tracks. Use WebAudio-generated or original placeholder loops. Add rubbery cat voices with per-cat pitch.


3. CATS
Seven stats: STR, DEX, CON, INT, CHA, SPD, LCK. Base stats range 3-7 (5 is neutral). Other cat data: sex (Male, Female or Neutral; about 10% are Neutral and can pair with anyone), age, libido, sexuality, hidden fertility, passives, active abilities, disorders, appearance genes, inbreeding value, lover and rival.
Derived stats:
- Max HP = CON x 4. Post-battle regen = 5 + floor((CON-5)/2) (equal to CON if below 5).
- Max mana = CHA x 3. Starting mana = CHA. Mana regen per turn = max(INT, 0).
- Movement range = max(1, 4 + trunc((SPD-5)/2)). Initiative = 2 x SPD (ties random).
- STR: +1 damage per point above 5 on melee basic attacks, +1 per 2 points above 5 on melee abilities.
- DEX: +1 damage per 2 points above 5 on ranged attacks and abilities.
- LCK: +2% crit chance per point above 5. Each point away from 5 also adds a 10% chance to roll an extra die for random outcomes (take the best result for high luck, the worst for low). It also improves shop quality, rewards and bonus-bird odds.
- Shield absorbs damage before HP and expires after battle. Holy Shield blocks whole hits.
- When a cat reaches 0 HP it is DOWNED and leaves a corpse with Corpse HP 3. Each heal or shield applied to the corpse adds +1 Corpse HP. If Corpse HP hits 0 the cat dies permanently. All downed cats revive after a won battle.
- Only BASE stats are inherited. Class bonuses, level-ups and gear bonuses are not.


4. HOUSE MODE
- Start with one room. NPC upgrades unlock more rooms (an attic, then rooms 2, 3 and 4).
- Furniture gives room stats:
  APPEAL (house-wide): better stats and ability variety on arriving stray cats.
  COMFORT: -1 per cat above 4 in a room. High Comfort means more overnight breeding. Low Comfort means more overnight fighting.
  STIMULATION: raises inheritance quality (see Breeding).
  HEALTH: slows aging, lowers old-age death chance, and gives cats a chance to recover from injuries and disorders overnight. Low Health gives hygiene problems.
  MUTATION: raises the chance cats develop mutations overnight.
- Day cycle: when you end the day, every cat ages 1. Each cat eats 1 food. If there isn't enough food, the starving cats get -1 to all stats, become aggressive, and may eat corpses or die. Then the end-of-day events run: breeding, fights (with injuries), strays arriving (age 2, 0% inbreeding), old-age deaths and mutations.
- Ages: 1 = kitten (cannot adventure). 2+ = young adult. Adults become OLD at a Health-based age threshold (as early as 5, as late as about 35). Old cats die overnight with roughly 11-21% chance depending on room Health, and get exhausted at battle round 5 instead of 10.
- Include a radio, a food inventory with capacity, an item storage with capacity, and a trash bin.
- Stretch goal: "house boss" events where cats defend the house against a named boss.


5. BREEDING (implement these rules exactly; they come from the community-datamined wiki)
Daily pairing:
1. Shuffle all living adults into per-room lists. Each cat acts as an initiator. (An Idol-of-Chastity-style furniture skips the attempt.)
2. The initiator picks a random partner in its room, weighted by compatibility.
3. Compatibility = 15% x initiator total CHA x partner libido (0-1) x lover_mult x sexuality_mult.
   - lover_mult: partner has no lover = 1. Initiator is the partner's lover = 1+affinity. Otherwise 1-affinity.
   - sexuality_mult: if either cat is Neutral, 1. Male+Female: cos(pi/2 x partner_sexuality). Same-sex: sin(pi/2 x partner_sexuality).
   - Cats with CHA <= 0 never initiate.
4. Make two rolls, each succeeding with chance compatibility x sqrt(1 + 0.1 x Comfort). Comfort <= -10 always fails. If roll 1 fails, skip this initiator. If roll 2 fails, remove both cats from today's candidates.
5. Assign father and mother roles by sex where possible (otherwise random). Recompute compatibility with the father as initiator. If it is below 5%, the partner rejects.
6. Result: Male-Male and Female-Female pairs make no kitten but raise the chance a special "gay stray" with bonus abilities (based on the breeders' classes) shows up. Other pairs make 1 kitten. Twin chance = (fatherFertility x motherFertility) - 1, where each fertility is hidden and between 1.0 and 1.25 (the lower of two random rolls).
7. Lovers: if a cat has no lover or affinity < 0.05, the partner becomes its lover at affinity 0.25. Otherwise affinity = 0.9a + 0.1 if the partner is the lover, or 0.9a if not. When a cat's lover breeds with someone else, that someone becomes that cat's rival (affinity 0.5, or 0.75a + 0.25 if already a rival). Rivals fight more.
Personality rolls at cat creation (not inherited): libido = the max of four random values in 0-50%, mirrored above 50% half the time. Sexuality is Straight (below 10%) 81.9% of the time, Bi 7.2%, and Gay (above 90%) 10.9%.


Kitten creation, in this order:
1. STATS: each of the 7 stats independently takes one parent's value. If room Stimulation > 0, the higher value is chosen with probability (100+Stim)/(200+Stim). If Stimulation < 0, the lower value is favored the same way.
2. ACTIVE ABILITIES: two independent attempts. Attempt 1 succeeds with chance 20% + 2.5% x Stim (guaranteed at 32). Attempt 2 succeeds with 2% + 0.5% x Stim (guaranteed at 196). A successful attempt picks a parent, then a random active ability from that parent.
3. PASSIVE: one attempt with chance 5% + 1% x Stim (guaranteed at 95).
4. DISORDERS: separate 15% roll per parent, each inheriting one random disorder from that parent. Stimulation does not affect this.
5. INBREEDING DISORDER: if the kitten has fewer than 2 disorders, chance max(2%, 0.4 x inbreeding% - 6%) to gain a birth-defect disorder.
6. APPEARANCE: for each of 15 body parts, inherit one parent's version. A mutation beats an ordinary part with probability 50% + 50% x Stim/(200+|Stim|). A birth defect is less likely to be inherited as Stimulation rises, and more likely as inbreeding rises.
7. 20% chance to reroll one random part group.
8. Symmetrize left and right parts (copy one side to the other, 50/50), so a kitten carries at most 10 inherited mutations.
9. Voice pitch: 98% inherited, 1% rerolled low, 1% rerolled high. Voice: 75% inherited, 25% rerolled.
10. BIRTH DEFECTS: only if inbreeding > 5%, with chance 1.5 x inbreeding% (guaranteed at about 66.6%). They can replace mutations but not other defects.
Inbreeding = kinship between the parents, computed recursively from shared ancestry (each generation up roughly halves the contribution; a cat's kinship with itself = (1 + its own inbreeding)/2). Strays are always 0%. Show tier icons: below 10% normal, 10-25% slight, 25-50% moderate, 50-80% high, above 80% extreme. Keep a family tree per cat.
Rule: a kitten can't be born with a base stat above 7 unless a positive mutation applies. Mutations typically give something like +2 to one stat and -1 to another. Mutation outcomes should be cosmetic-plus-mechanical, and cats with them can be submitted to an NPC for rewards.
Build a debug panel that simulates 1,000 kittens from two chosen parents and a Stimulation value, so I can verify the distributions.


6. ADVENTURE STRUCTURE
- Party: 1-4 non-retired adult cats. Flow: Class Selection (assign collars, then "Lock In!" irreversibly), then the Equip Screen (5 slots per cat: weapon, head, neck, face, trinket or consumable; up to 20 items per party; "Lock In!" again), then the Act screen. There is no turning back until the chapter boss is dealt with.
- Each Act has 3 chapters, with branching routes and a hidden final area. Chapters are mostly linear strings of NODES: Battle, Event (random "?" events), Treasure, Shop, Miniboss, Boss and House (ends the run). The sequence of nodes is the same each time, but node contents are random and chapter-themed.
- HARD PATH: roughly halfway through chapters 1-3 an optional harder branch appears (after the first Sewers clear). It has an extra battle, at least 2 "Champion" enemies per fight, rarer treasure, and better rewards.
- Rewards per battle: coins (party carries max 99 per run), food, a chance at an item or consumable, and ONE level-up for the party's lowest-level cat. Rarity roll for item rewards: 50/101 common, 40/101 uncommon, 10/101 rare, 1/101 very rare. Each reward has a 50/50 chance to come from the general pool or the chapter-specific pool.
- Shops always sell a Rare Candy for 10 coins (instantly levels a cat) plus 2-4 items. Shop quality scales with party Luck.
- Items equipped at embark become WORN, with a 50% chance to break when you return home. Money bags and furniture boxes found on a run convert into coins and furniture at home.
- If a cat permanently dies mid-run, events can offer a level-0 replacement cat. Rare events give extra follower cats beyond the 4-cat limit.
- Failure: you lose everything. An NPC (the Organ Grinder) later lets you recover a share of coins/food or one item, and levels up on its own from your failed runs.
- Unlocks: clear both chapter-3 endings in Act 1 to unlock Act 2, and both in Act 2 to unlock Act 3.


7. COMBAT (turn-based, 10x10 grid)
- Each tile has 5 layers: Unit, Gas, Pickup, Trap and Tile-Type. Player cats start on one of 4 possible tiles (assigned randomly). Large enemies occupy several tiles.
- Battles run in ROUNDS. Each unit takes a turn in initiative order. Turn order is dynamic: speed buffs and extra turns can change it mid-round. Enemies can also have bonus turns, shown as ">" markers.
- Each turn a unit has: 1 move action, 1 basic attack (melee or ranged, no mana cost), 1 weapon use, 1 trinket/consumable use, and any number of spells that cost mana. At the start of the turn, actions refresh and start-of-turn effects apply. At the end of the turn, gain mana and health regen and apply end-of-turn effects.
- Cats can have at most 4 active abilities and 2 passives.
- EXHAUSTION: starts at round 10 (round 5 for Old cats). Exhausted cats take stacking unblockable damage each turn, and have their healing and mana gain reduced. Final-chapter boss fights give Adrenaline instead (+25% crit, +25% block, exhaustion held at 0).
- AMBUSH: some events or items let one side act in "round 0".
- FACTIONS: allies, enemies, solitary/mad enemies (hostile to everyone), neutral birds, third-party teams, and weather-triggered "uprising" factions (birds, aliens, robots, ghosts). Factions have alliance rules and some enemies can be charmed, mind-controlled or possessed.
- BONUS BIRDS: base 20% chance per battle, boosted by party Luck. They are neutral, hunted by allies, and ignored by enemies. Killing one gives its killer +1 all stats and a bonus item.
- Directional damage: backstabs deal extra damage. Knockback can push units into hazards, pits, traps or other units.
- Crits, dodge, block and miss exist. Dodge chances are independent rolls and don't add up.
- Victory when all required enemies are dead or fled. Defeat when all party cats are downed.
- Enemy AI is simple and legible: each enemy type has a few behaviors (pounce, multi-hit melee, ranged, summon, knock-up, heal) and a visible tooltip. Always show hit chances, damage previews and the turn-order bar (ally, enemy, boss and bonus icons).


8. ELEMENTS, TERRAIN, STATUSES, WEATHER
Elements: Electric, Fire, Ice, Water, Grass, Earth, Wind, Holy, Explosion, Gravity, Music. Mages and others can attune: casting an elemental spell empowers your basic attack with that element for the rest of the battle.
Key interactions (implement as data-driven rules):
- Water or Wet extinguishes Fire and cures Burn, and turns Fire tiles into Water.
- Fire burns Grass, Web and Tar tiles, and melts Ice into Water.
- Ice on Water makes Ice tiles; Ice on Wet units inflicts Freeze; Ice on Grass makes damaging Ice Spikes; Ice on Burning units deals bonus damage.
- Electric on Water tiles or Wet units causes an AoE electrocution. Wet units are vulnerable to Electric and Ice.
- Holy healing damages Undead units.

PROJECT: "Cat Lineage" (working title) — a tactical cat-breeding roguelite

Build a playable browser game (HTML5 + TypeScript/JS; Phaser 3, PixiJS or plain Canvas, your choice) that recreates the core design of Mewgenics (Edmund McMillen and Tyler Glaiel, released Feb 10, 2026). This is a personal fan-style prototype. Reproduce the SYSTEMS, structure and FEEL, but make all art, audio, text and character names ORIGINAL. Do not copy or trace the original game's assets or lines. Support desktop mouse and mobile touch.


HOW TO WORK
- Start with a short plan and list your assumptions. Don't ask me questions; decide and document.
- Build in the milestone order at the bottom. After each milestone, run it, fix bugs, and tell me what is done and what is stubbed.
- Make everything data-driven (JSON for classes, abilities, items, statuses, tiles, enemies, events, furniture). Keep simulation logic in pure functions, separate from rendering. Use a seeded RNG.
- Put every tunable constant in one config file.


1. THE PITCH AND CORE LOOP
You move into a small fictional town (call it "Boon County") and raise a lineage of cats in a cluttered house. The game has two halves:
- HOUSE (management and breeding sim): place furniture, feed cats, let them breed and fight overnight, manage room stats.
- ADVENTURE (turn-based tactics roguelite): send a party of 1-4 adult cats through chapters of battles, events, shops and bosses.
Loop: breed -> assign class collars and equip items -> adventure -> loot -> cats that return become RETIRED (cannot adventure again) -> donate cats to NPCs for permanent upgrades -> breed the next generation. If the whole party dies, all cats, items and resources on that run are lost.
Tone: dark, crude, absurd humor (poop jokes, grotesque mutations, deadpan NPCs), but cats stay expressive and endearing. Keep it PG-13: breeding happens off-screen as a cheeky text log ("X got together with Y and made a kitten!"), with no explicit animation.


2. ART DIRECTION (very important)
Reference: Edmund McMillen's The Binding of Isaac, Super Meat Boy and The End Is Nigh, and Newgrounds-era Flash cartoons (Clubby the Seal, the Obituary-era look). The game is described as crude, Flash-animated vector art with bold lines and bulbous, grotesque-but-cute characters. Reviewers also note a mostly black-and-white feel with small color accents.
- Linework: thick, slightly wobbly black outlines, uneven line weight, hand-drawn imperfection. Add a subtle line-wobble effect.
- Shapes: bulbous, rubbery, over-round bodies; huge expressive eyes and eyebrows; stubby limbs; weird-but-readable silhouettes.
- Animation: Flash-style puppet rigs. Cats are built from swappable vector parts (body, head, tail, legs, arms, eyes, eyebrows, ears, mouth, fur texture) with tweened squash-and-stretch, idle breathing, blinking and exaggerated hit reactions. Boss animations should feel slick and bigger than normal enemies.
- Palette: dingy paper off-white (#EDE6D6), soot black (#151210), dried-blood red (#B3261E), bile yellow (#D9B84A), sickly green (#7C8F3A), bruise purple (#5B3A6B). Use mostly desaturated backgrounds and let color pop on cats, status effects and hazards.
- House: cozy cross-section rooms crammed with junk furniture, with a radio, food bowls and litter.
- Battle: a readable 10x10 tile grid with clean icons. Tile types need distinct silhouettes and colors, because bold lines and bulbous characters can make the board hard to read.
- Mutations visibly change body parts (extra eyes, weird ears, bandaged mouths, odd tails).
- NOT: clean corporate flat vector, glossy 3D, pixel art, anime.
Audio and tone: each chapter gets its own energetic, melodic, genre-hopping theme with a punny title, and the house has a radio station with unlockable tracks. Use WebAudio-generated or original placeholder loops. Add rubbery cat voices with per-cat pitch.


3. CATS
Seven stats: STR, DEX, CON, INT, CHA, SPD, LCK. Base stats range 3-7 (5 is neutral). Other cat data: sex (Male, Female or Neutral; about 10% are Neutral and can pair with anyone), age, libido, sexuality, hidden fertility, passives, active abilities, disorders, appearance genes, inbreeding value, lover and rival.
Derived stats:
- Max HP = CON x 4. Post-battle regen = 5 + floor((CON-5)/2) (equal to CON if below 5).
- Max mana = CHA x 3. Starting mana = CHA. Mana regen per turn = max(INT, 0).
- Movement range = max(1, 4 + trunc((SPD-5)/2)). Initiative = 2 x SPD (ties random).
- STR: +1 damage per point above 5 on melee basic attacks, +1 per 2 points above 5 on melee abilities.
- DEX: +1 damage per 2 points above 5 on ranged attacks and abilities.
- LCK: +2% crit chance per point above 5. Each point away from 5 also adds a 10% chance to roll an extra die for random outcomes (take the best result for high luck, the worst for low). It also improves shop quality, rewards and bonus-bird odds.
- Shield absorbs damage before HP and expires after battle. Holy Shield blocks whole hits.
- When a cat reaches 0 HP it is DOWNED and leaves a corpse with Corpse HP 3. Each heal or shield applied to the corpse adds +1 Corpse HP. If Corpse HP hits 0 the cat dies permanently. All downed cats revive after a won battle.
- Only BASE stats are inherited. Class bonuses, level-ups and gear bonuses are not.


4. HOUSE MODE
- Start with one room. NPC upgrades unlock more rooms (an attic, then rooms 2, 3 and 4).
- Furniture gives room stats:
  APPEAL (house-wide): better stats and ability variety on arriving stray cats.
  COMFORT: -1 per cat above 4 in a room. High Comfort means more overnight breeding. Low Comfort means more overnight fighting.
  STIMULATION: raises inheritance quality (see Breeding).
  HEALTH: slows aging, lowers old-age death chance, and gives cats a chance to recover from injuries and disorders overnight. Low Health gives hygiene problems.
  MUTATION: raises the chance cats develop mutations overnight.
- Day cycle: when you end the day, every cat ages 1. Each cat eats 1 food. If there isn't enough food, the starving cats get -1 to all stats, become aggressive, and may eat corpses or die. - Ages: 1 = kitten (cannot adventure). 2+ = young adult. Adults become OLD at a Health-based age threshold (as early as 5, as late as about 35). Old cats die overnight with roughly 11-21% chance depending on room Health, and get exhausted at battle round 5 instead of 10.
- Include a radio, a food inventory with capacity, an item storage with capacity, and a trash bin.
- Stretch goal: "house boss" events where cats defend the house against a named boss.


5. BREEDING (implement these rules exactly; they come from the community-datamined wiki)
Daily pairing:
1. Shuffle all living adults into per-room lists. Each cat acts as an initiator. (An Idol-of-Chastity-style furniture skips the attempt.)
2. The initiator picks a random partner in its room, weighted by compatibility.
3. Compatibility = 15% x initiator total CHA x partner libido (0-1) x lover_mult x sexuality_mult.
   - lover_mult: partner has no lover = 1. Initiator is the partner's lover = 1+affinity. Otherwise 1-affinity.

   - Cats with CHA <= 0 never initiate.
4. Make two rolls, each succeeding with chance compatibility x sqrt(1 + 0.1 x Comfort). Comfort <= -10 always fails. If roll 1 fails, skip this initiator. If roll 2 fails, remove both cats from today's candidates.
5. Assign father and mother roles by sex where possible (otherwise random). Recompute compatibility with the father as initiator. If it is below 5%, the partner rejects.
6. Result: Male-Male and Female-Female pairs make no kitten but raise the chance a special "gay stray" with bonus abilities (based on the breeders' classes) shows up. Other pairs make 1 kitten. 7. Lovers: if a cat has no lover or affinity < 0.05, the partner becomes its lover at affinity 0.25. Otherwise affinity = 0.9a + 0.1 if the partner is the lover, or 0.9a if not. Personality rolls at cat creation (not inherited): libido = the max of four random values in 0-50%, mirrored above 50% half the time. Sexuality is Straight (below 10%) 81.9% of the time, Bi 7.2%, and Gay (above 90%) 10.9%.


Kitten creation, in this order:
1. STATS: each of the 7 stats independently takes one parent's value. If room Stimulation > 0, the higher value is chosen with probability (100+Stim)/(200+Stim). If Stimulation < 0, the lower value is favored the same way.
2. ACTIVE ABILITIES: two independent attempts. Attempt 1 succeeds with chance 20% + 2.5% x Stim (guaranteed at 32). Attempt 2 succeeds with 2% + 0.5% x Stim (guaranteed at 196). A successful attempt picks a parent, then a random active ability from that parent.
3. PASSIVE: one attempt with chance 5% + 1% x Stim (guaranteed at 95).
4. DISORDERS: separate 15% roll per parent, each inheriting one random disorder from that parent. Stimulation does not affect this.
5. INBREEDING DISORDER: if the kitten has fewer than 2 disorders, chance max(2%, 0.4 x inbreeding% - 6%) to gain a birth-defect disorder.
6. APPEARANCE: for each of 15 body parts, inherit one parent's version. A mutation beats an ordinary part with probability 50% + 50% x Stim/(200+|Stim|). A birth defect is less likely to be inherited as Stimulation rises, and more likely as inbreeding rises.
7. 20% chance to reroll one random part group.
8. Symmetrize left and right parts (copy one side to the other, 50/50), so a kitten carries at most 10 inherited mutations.
9. Voice pitch: 98% inherited, 1% rerolled low, 1% rerolled high. Voice: 75% inherited, 25% rerolled.
10. BIRTH DEFECTS: only if inbreeding > 5%, with chance 1.5 x inbreeding% (guaranteed at about 66.6%). They can replace mutations but not other defects.
Inbreeding = kinship between the parents, computed recursively from shared ancestry (each generation up roughly halves the contribution; a cat's kinship with itself = (1 + its own inbreeding)/2). Strays are always 0%. Show tier icons: below 10% normal, 10-25% slight, 25-50% moderate, 50-80% high, above 80% extreme. Keep a family tree per cat.
Rule: a kitten can't be born with a base stat above 7 unless a positive mutation applies. Mutations typically give something like +2 to one stat and -1 to another. Mutation outcomes should be cosmetic-plus-mechanical, and cats with them can be submitted to an NPC for rewards.

- Farmhand/builder (reference: Frank): accepts any retired cat; unlocks more rooms at 1/25/60/100 donated cats.
- Breeding scientist neighbor (reference: Tink): accepts kittens; each batch of 10 reveals more cat info (base stats, inbreeding, orientation and libido icons, aggression, love/hate icons); after 60 kittens, further donations give coins.
- Shopkeeper (reference: Tracy): accepts cats aged 5+; sells food storage boxes and up to 3 Blank Collars (duplicate random unlocked classes).
- Combat instructor (reference: Butch): accepts adventured cats in batches of 20; expands item storage and hands out class collars after chapter clears.
- Mad doctor (reference: Dr. Beanies): accepts batches of 5 cats with mutations, defects or disorders; unlocks "invention" side quests (max 5 active) that make runs harder for loot; quest items are lost if the carrier dies.

Act 1 (grounded): Alley -> Sewers or Junkyard -> Caves or Boneyard -> hidden Throbbing Domain.
Act 2 (extreme): Desert -> Bunker or Crater -> Core or Moon -> hidden Rift.
Act 3 (time travel): Lab -> Ice Age or Future -> Jurassic or End -> hidden Infinite.
Each chapter needs a theme song, enemy roster, tile hazards, item pool, miniboss and boss. Examples: Sewers have Water tiles that slow movement; the Moon has astronauts, living asteroids and aliens; the Ice Age has cavemen, sabertooth cats and mammoths that fight each other.

Tactical overview toggle, right-click or long-press tooltips, tappable stat sheet, family tree and inbreeding icon, two-step "Lock In!" screens, level-up modal, event modal, a turn-order bar, a save button (paper icon), and a clear end-day button. All text legible at phone size.

M1: Cat generator, vector body-part renderer with mutations, stat sheet, name and voice generator.
M2: Combat sandbox: 10x10 grid, turn order, movement, basic attacks, mana, 4 classes (Fighter, Hunter, Mage, Cleric) with ~8 abilities each, 5 statuses, 3 elements, and basic enemy AI.

M6: Sewers and Junkyard chapters, hard path, remaining Act 1 classes, weather, disorders and mutations.
M7: Polish: audio, juice, tutorial, balancing pass.

## Objective
- Build an original, playable browser cat-breeding roguelite set in Boon County, covering the M1–M4 loop: breed cats, equip collars, explore the Alley, return or lose, retire survivors, breed again, and persist saves.

## Requirements
- Use original art, text, characters, and audio; support desktop and mobile; do not copy source-game assets or lines.
- Keep simulation separate from rendering, use seeded RNG, store tunable constants in one config file, and make game content data-driven JSON.
- Follow milestone order and report what is complete or stubbed after each; do not ask questions.
- Broader M5–M7 scope includes NPC/meta progression, more chapters/classes/items/statuses, a debug breeding simulator, and polish/audio.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with generated SVG art and WebAudio/original placeholder audio.
- Prioritize a compact playable slice and document the single-player prototype assumption.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive app shell, styles, configuration, and starter content in `index.html`, `style.css`, `config.json`, and `content.json`.
- Implemented seeded RNG, starter cats, generated SVG cat/enemy rendering, house/battle views, and localStorage persistence.
- Implemented preliminary battle encounters, events, rewards, retirement/loss handling, party/collar controls, cat inspection, breeding, feeding, furniture repair, end-day behavior, and help/radio interactions.
- Fixed the missing `enemySvg` declaration; `node --input-type=module --check < game.js` now passes.
- Verified the app’s initial house screen renders in headless Chromium at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`.

### Active
- Test the full gameplay interactions in a browser and fix any runtime or flow issues.
- Compare implementation against M1–M4 and report completed features versus simplifications/stubs.

### Blocked
- Full interactive browser testing remains unverified; headless testing so far only confirmed the initial render.

## Next Move
1. Exercise house actions, breeding, collar and party selection, battle movement/attacks/skills, victory/defeat, retirement, and save/load in Chromium.
2. Fix any discovered interaction or runtime issues.
3. Report M1–M4 completion and remaining stubs, distinguishing implemented features from simplifications.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: state, rendering, simulation, breeding, interactions, and save/load.
- `index.html`: app shell and JavaScript entry point.
- `style.css`: responsive layout and visual styling.
- `config.json`: tunable constants.
- `content.json`: starter classes, items, statuses, tiles, enemies, events, furniture, and music titles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing class IDs are `scrapper`, `mender`, `slink`, and `oracle`.
- `config.json` currently sets `partyLimit` to 4.
- The local HTTP server on port 8765 and Chromium remote-debugging process on port 9222 were started for browser testing.

## Objective
- Complete and verify the original playable Boon County cat-breeding roguelite’s M1–M4 slice, then report implemented features versus simplifications and stubs.

## Requirements
- Use original content and art; support desktop and mobile.
- Separate simulation from rendering, use seeded RNG, centralize tunables in `config.json`, and keep content data-driven in `content.json`.
- Follow milestone order; do not ask questions.
- Broader scope includes NPC/meta progression, more chapters/classes/items/statuses, a debug breeding simulator, and polish/audio.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with generated SVG art, localStorage saves, and placeholder radio/audio behavior.
- Prioritize a compact playable slice and document the single-player prototype assumption.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive house and battle views, seeded simulation, generated SVG art, localStorage saves, breeding, feeding, furniture repair, party/collar controls, encounters, events, and boss combat.
- Fixed movement highlighting so junk tiles are not marked as reachable.
- Browser-tested house actions, all four party members, the three-encounter run through the boss, successful loot extraction/retirement, and save persistence after reload; no runtime exceptions surfaced.
- Verified `node --input-type=module --check < game.js` passes.

### Active
- Summarize M1–M4 coverage and distinguish implemented features from simplifications and stubs.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Report verified implementation and remaining simplifications/stubs.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Simulation, rendering, breeding, encounters, combat, and save/load.
- `config.json`: Tunable constants.
- `content.json`: Classes, items, statuses, tiles, enemies, events, and starter content.
- `/tmp/opencode/test-full.cjs`: Chromium CDP test covering the full run and reload persistence.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Full-run browser test finished at home with `winCount: 1`, four retired cats, loot banked (`food: 13`, `scrap: 9`), and the same state after reload.
- The full-run test confirmed zero junk tiles had movement highlights and captured no browser exceptions.
- `content.json` includes item and status definitions, but their gameplay integration should be treated as unverified; the radio control is placeholder behavior rather than verified audio playback.
- Broader NPC/meta progression, additional chapters/content, debug breeding simulator, and polish/audio remain outside the verified slice.

## M1–M4 slice: implemented and verified

- **Foundation and home:** Responsive standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally generated SVG cat and enemy art. Simulation logic and rendering are separated in `game.js`; tunables are in `config.json`, and content definitions are in `content.json`. Saves persist in browser `localStorage`.
- **Household and breeding:** Cat roster, class/collar selection, party selection, feeding, furniture repair, end-of-day growth, strays, and breeding. Breeding creates kittens with inherited stats, possible mutations, and family links.
- **Turn-based combat:** A 10×10 battle grid with movement and attack ranges, obstacles, cover, hazards, enemy turns, class skills, and selectable cats. I fixed movement highlighting so impassable junk tiles aren’t shown as reachable.
- **Expedition progression:** Three encounters, event choices, a boss fight against Mayor Mold, loot extraction or continued risk, and retirement of cats that return successfully. Losing the party ends the run and removes those cats.
- **Verification:** JavaScript syntax check passed. A browser test exercised household actions, a full successful run through the boss, loot extraction, and reload persistence. The saved win, retired party, and banked resources were present after reload; the test captured no browser exceptions.

## Simplifications and remaining work

- This is a **compact, single-player prototype**, not the broader progression game. It has one expedition route and one boss; there’s no implemented NPC/meta-progression system, additional chapters, or debug breeding simulator.
- Combat XP is recorded during a run, but persistent leveling and a broader advancement system aren’t implemented. Item and status definitions exist in `content.json`, but their gameplay integration is unverified; there’s no verified item acquisition/equipment loop, and statuses are not part of the tested combat flow.
- Events are simple choices with small food/scrap rewards or no reward. Furniture repair changes household comfort and mood rather than providing a deeper furniture system.
- The radio is a **placeholder**: it displays track names and toggles UI state, but does not play audio.
- The game uses local browser saves rather than accounts or a backend. The layout includes responsive styling, but mobile-device behavior was not part of the recorded browser test.

Project files remain uncommitted and appear as untracked in Git.
